criterion: 3 — a .py or .R row that is short (≤ 120 lines) or marked as a notebook (`# %%` cells, or `# notebook` in its first lines) is converted once … and opened in JupyterLab; longer code opens in the editor … and the row says which
message: P1.1 HOLDs the entire `open_kind` module until John re-ratifies that a long `# %%` / `# notebook` file opens as a notebook. Criterion 3 already locks that marker rule, and the quote independently locks the short/long split. Packaging the override beside the classifier parks both. With no classifier, no row can say "notebook" / "editor", and a 20-line `.py` has no decision that sends it to a notebook. The operator's first visible distinction is gated on a question the North Star already answered.

criterion: 1 — a project's own JupyterLab, managed like a preview: started on demand (cwd = the project folder) on an OS-assigned free port that is never 8777, with its own token, registered, listed, stoppable, reaped when dead
message: P2.1 spends zero until John picks (A) the existing jupyter-serve or (B) a new per-project lab. Criterion 1 is (B). The HOLD then parks start/probe/ensure, `fake_lab`, the labs endpoints, the boot reap, and the `/notebook` 302 Location. There is no operator-visible fallback: no project lab, no stop control, no restart of a dead lab. Re-asking the North Star as a one-liner leaves criterion 1 unimplemented while later phases still talk as if a lab exists.

criterion: 2 — a .ipynb row (register, plan outline, files tile) opens in a new window at the lab's /lab/tree/<rel> for that file, starting or restarting the lab if needed — never a blank page
message: Phase 3 KEEPs `open_kind` on register rows, the delivRow `/notebook` rewrite, and files-tile `window.open` of that route. Phase 2's lab dispatch, `ensure_lab`, and never-blank interstitial are HOLD. John will see a chip and a clickable row. One implementation reads the KEEP list and ships hrefs at a missing or half-built route (blank/404/hung tab). The other skips the rewrite because `open_kind` never shipped, so the same rows stay read-only artifacts. Either way a notebook row does not open in JupyterLab. The plan has no operator contract for what a click does while those HOLDs stand.

criterion: 2 — a stale or dead lab is restarted, never a blank page
message: The interstitial is HOLD until "a recorded click that is blank or hung under a blocking 302-after-probe." Criterion 2 already forbids that click. Remaining path is a GET `/notebook` that waits up to 20s for a probe, then 302s or errors — a spinnerless tab on the dashboard origin, which is a blank page. The rebuild trigger makes John the first failing test instead of treating never-blank as a ship rule. A lab that is "up on first probe" skips the page; the cold start, the missing-jupyter case, and the hung pid are exactly when he clicks.

criterion: 5 — a live-link row opens (Playwright screenshots); 4 — a Where cell that is a localhost / 127.0.0.1 / tailnet-name URL renders as a link (new window) (journal 0110 — a JupyterLab or Shiny address reachable from the register and the plan without a launch page)
message: Sign-off (d) only asserts the row is an `<a>` whose href has no `token=` and whose rel contains noopener, then screenshots that. It does not navigate. Criterion 5 says the live-link row opens. Criterion 4's 0110 clause is reachable, not merely painted. A screenshot of a link is the launch-page workaround in thinner clothing: John still cannot tell whether the address works. The fixture `http://gwl-server:<lab port or 8888>/lab` cannot even be written honestly — the lab port is OS-assigned at start, and 8888 is not that lab.

criterion: 4 — a Where cell that is a http://<this machine's tailnet name>/… URL renders as a link (new window); journal 0110 — a JupyterLab address reachable from the register without a launch page
section: Phase 1 bind + Phase 3 stale-by-design + Phase 4 fixture
message: The managed lab binds `--ip=127.0.0.1` with `allow_remote_access=False`; tailnet bind is explicitly deferred. Phase 3 then KEEPs `where_for(url=)` so a campaign can register a JupyterLab address, and parks current-port rendering with "a registered lab URL may go stale, by design." Phase 5 still uses a `gwl-server` live-link as the proof row. That hostname will not connect to a loopback-only lab, and an OS-assigned port baked into DELIVERABLES.md is dead on the next start. This is the 0110 dead JupyterLab address, now as a specified outcome. Path-rows via `/notebook` do not save a Where cell that is the URL criterion 4 exists to make clickable.

criterion: 3 — longer code opens in the editor (VS Code on this machine, `code -r <file>`); 5 — a long .py opens in the editor (Playwright screenshots)
message: Criterion 3 names `code -r`. The editor element still dual-fires `location.assign(vscode://file/<abs>)` and the editor seam; vscode:// is HOLD until a recorded click where `code -r` failed. Sign-off (c) then captures a `vscode://file/` navigation request and screenshots that browser page, and defers proving VS Code raised the file as a human glance. The operator proof is the HOLD URI on a tab that says "Opening … in the editor," not the editor window. Dual-fire, if the URI leaks through, can also open the file twice. The North Star editor path is unshown.

criterion: 2 — starting or restarting the lab if needed — never a blank page; a stale or dead lab is restarted
message: `ensure_lab` treats a live pid whose `/api/status` probe fails twice as dead, tree-kills it, and starts fresh, with a 20s health timeout. Criterion 2 restarts stale or dead labs, not slow ones. A cold JupyterLab on this machine that is still binding when the probe expires is killed mid-boot. The next click starts another. The file is never selected; with P3.3 HOLD there is no progress page, only a hung `/notebook` tab. Restart-on-hung becomes restart-on-not-ready-yet, which is how "come up every time" becomes "never stays up."

criterion: 3 — kernel python3 or ir; Statement — short code as a Jupyter notebook in the project's own JupyterLab (Python and R kernels)
section: Phase 1 deferred / Phase 0 writer / Phase 4 sign-off
message: `to_notebook` stamps `.R` with kernelspec `ir`. R kernel install is deferred. Sign-off skips the `.R` row if IRkernel is absent, "honestly." The operator who clicks a short `.R` still gets a sibling notebook that names a kernel the lab does not have. Execution-on-open is a non-goal; shipping an R kernel in the lab is not — the statement is Python and R kernels, not Python plus an `ir` label. A skipped sign-off row is not an R open. The row's "notebook" chip will lie about where that file runs.

criterion: 3 — converted once to a sibling one-cell .ipynb
message: Criterion 3 is one-cell. P1.3 HOLD says omit `marker_split` from `to_notebook`, the route, and the tests. The near-term text still specifies `marker_split=True`, a Judge flag, shared-writer both-paths, tests for both, and P3.2 still passes the flag into the route. An implementer following the phase body builds per-cell conversion for `# %%` files; one following the HOLD table does not. John clicking a marked file cannot know whether he gets one cell or many. A HOLD that leaves the spend in the spec is not a cut. One-cell is already locked — the leftover flag is unearned operator-visible behaviour.

criterion: 1 — a project's own JupyterLab, managed like a preview (cwd = project folder, OS-assigned port never 8777, own token, registered, listed, stoppable, reaped)
message: The locked criterion is a per-project lab with preview discipline. The plan still specifies `lab_server.py`, then HOLDs it and every dependent (ensure/probe, fake_lab, labs endpoints, Lab chip, 127.0.0.1 Location) until John picks (A) existing jupyter-serve or (B) a new lab — and says spend zero until (B). Option (A) is not criterion 1: it is not per-project, not cwd = the project folder, not an OS-assigned port, not registered/listed/stoppable/reaped like a preview. A Master Plan that leaves the substrate as a Stage-0 rewrite cannot deliver the surface. The KEEP’d work (classifier, chips, href rewrite) does not make a lab come up.

criterion: 2 — starting or restarting the lab if needed; a stale or dead lab is restarted, never a blank page
section: Phase 2 — ensure_lab wait vs immediate interstitial (P3.3 / P3.7 HOLD)
message: The same paragraph requires `ensure_lab` to wait up to 20 s for a probe AND the route to answer IMMEDIATELY with a poll page. It does not say who starts the lab if the wait is not on the request thread, and it HOLDs both the interstitial and `lab_ready` until a recorded hung click. What remains is a blocking 302-after-probe. A cold JupyterLab boot is then a silent 20 s tab — the blank page criterion 2 forbids. Stub `fake_lab` answers at once, so no test in Phases 0–3 ever sees a real boot. Premortem 1 is claimed closed in prose and HOLD’d in the table.

criterion: 2 — opens in a new window at the lab's /lab/tree/<rel> for that file (starting the lab if needed)
message: Kind-dispatch is KEEP’d; the Location it 302s to is HOLD’d. If (B), the click goes to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/lab/tree/…` of a lab the plan is not yet allowed to spawn. If (A), `/lab/tree/<rel>` is relative to jupyter-serve’s root, not the project folder, so an in-effort notebook is a 404 or the wrong tree — and nothing starts or restarts a dead lab. Criterion 2 is one click that lands on that file in that project’s lab. This route as HOLD’d has no such target.

criterion: 5 — on a real project a .ipynb row opens the lab with the file selected, a short .py opens as a notebook, a long .py opens in the editor, a live-link row opens (Playwright screenshots)
message: The four screenshots do not measure the four claims. (a) “file selected” is a document title or tab-label `or`, which a JupyterLab shell with the path only in the URL can satisfy. (c) asserts a `vscode://file/` navigation while criterion 3 names `code -r <file>` and P3.5 HOLDs the URI handler — so the live gate proves a path the plan itself parked. (d) asserts `href` has no `token=` and `rel` contains noopener; it never follows the link. The live-link row is `http://gwl-server:<lab port or 8888>/lab` while Phase 1 binds `--ip=127.0.0.1` and `allow_remote_access=False`, so that host:port is not the managed lab (and 8888 is a guess). Criterion 5 is eyes on the opens, not attribute lints plus a PNG.

criterion: 3 — longer code opens in the editor (VS Code on this machine, `code -r <file>`), and the row says which
message: The locked launcher is `code -r <file>`. The overview, the editor page, and the sign-off all dual-fire `vscode://file/<abs>` plus the seam, which can open the file twice and put an absolute path in history. P3.5 HOLDs the URI half “until a recorded click where `code -r` did not land,” while Phase 4 still requires a `vscode://` href to pass. Criterion 3 is satisfied by a non-blocking `code -r` that actually raises the file. The extra scheme is not in the criterion, and the gate that is supposed to see the editor is wired to the parked half.

criterion: 4 — a Where cell that is http://localhost, 127.0.0.1, or this machine's tailnet name renders as a link; every other host stays text
message: Production resolution of “this machine’s tailnet name” is `socket.gethostname()` (this host’s friendly name is not guaranteed to be the tailnet name), plus a 2 s `tailscale status --self --json` subprocess, plus an unset `ANCHOR_TAILNET_NAMES`. Tests inject the env and stub the binary. The register is served by the NSSM `anchor` process, whose PATH has already been the reason external CLIs vanish. If the probe fails, `http://gwl-server/…` and the friction-note FQDN stay text — journal 0110 unfixed on the live service. Criterion 4 is a row John can click, not a stubbed frozenset. The allowlist needs a durable, service-visible name list, not a best-effort spawn.

criterion: 3 — short (≤ 120 lines) or marked as a notebook (`# %%` cells, or `# notebook` in its first lines)
message: One sentence specifies two incompatible scans: “the first 5 non-blank lines for `# %%`” and “anywhere in the file counts as a cell marker, scanned up to the 121-line cap.” A 100-line file with `# %%` on line 50 is editor under the first rule and notebook under the second. The stub table pins “`# %%` on line 3 of a 400-line file → notebook,” which is a third case (long + marker). P1.1 then HOLDs that third case until John re-ratifies text already in the locked criterion (“short OR marked”). A classifier with two windows and a HOLD on the criterion’s own marker clause will not render the same chip the route executes.

criterion: 3 — converted once to a sibling one-cell .ipynb
section: Phase 0 — to_notebook (P1.2 KEEP / P1.3 HOLD) and Phase 2 dispatch
message: Criterion 3 is one-cell. P1.3 HOLD says omit `marker_split` from the writer, the route, and the tests. P1.2 KEEP still takes `marker_split=False`, the Judge-flag paragraph still tests both paths, and P3.2 still passes `marker_split=<Judge flag>`. A HOLD that leaves the flag on the KEEP’d signature is a split converter Foreman will implement. That is not one-cell, and it is not a cut.

criterion: 3 — a .py or .R row … kernel python3 or ir; statement — JupyterLab (Python and R kernels)
section: Phase 1 deferred “R kernel install” / Phase 4 fixture
message: The statement requires Python and R kernels in the project lab. The plan writes `ir` into JSON and defers installing or detecting IRkernel. Phase 4’s live list is ipynb / short .py / long .py / live-link; the `.R` row is “skipped honestly if IRkernel is missing.” Criterion 5 was the gate that would have caught a kernel-less R open; it was written to omit R. An `.R` click can therefore ship as a notebook whose kernel is absent — open, not where it runs. Execution-on-open is a non-goal; shipping R as an untested metadata tag is not.

criterion: 2 — a .ipynb in the register, under its step in the plan, or in the files tile opens at /lab/tree/<rel>
message: Files-tile clicks are `window.open` of `/notebook` with `dir=''` and “the path is project-relative there.” The plan does not say the files payload actually carries project-root-relative paths. If a produced file is effort-relative (the register’s `dir` exists for that reason), `dir=''` joins to a path that fails the containment check or 404s, and the files tile is the one surface that never starts the lab on the right file. Criterion 2 names that tile. Register and plan inherit `dir`; files are specified as if they do not need it, without a proof that the producer agrees.

criterion: 3 — the row says which ("notebook" / "editor")
message: The locked labels are notebook and editor. The chip also prints `lab` for `.ipynb`. That is a third word the criterion does not use, so a notebook row does not “say which” in the vocabulary the surface locked. Harmless if renamed; as specified it fails the letter of criterion 3 on the most common row.
